dossier.headline: India-US trade deal nears the finish line as new US tariffs loom
dossier.summary: The US has proposed tariffs on 14 trading partners, with India facing 17% if it signs a trade deal and 25% without one. India has rejected a US excess-capacity charge and is pushing for an early deal, and on 27 November Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said talks are close to culmination.
why_it_matters: A deal would cap US tariffs on Indian goods at 17% rather than 25%
The 17% rate is below those proposed for Vietnam, Malaysia and Bangladesh
Analysts have linked some of the IT sector's weakness to tariff concerns
watch: Whether a signed deal or joint statement follows Goyal's comments
The US finalising its new tariff framework, on which signing depends
Public hearings on the proposal; no levy can start before January 2027

Will the 17% rate hold once the US framework is final?
